newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Spirit of HK handover in bow ties, boats and bed.
newsitem.headline: Spirit of HK handover in bow ties, boats and bed.

text.p: Sir Donald Tsang, Hong Kong's dapper Financial Secretary, disclosed on Wednesday why he wears bow ties -- it's because he's short, a messy eater and prefers to spend less on his neckwear.

In an interview with Reuters, the diminutive Tsang said: "It's a practical problem. I'm short, and I'm a messy eater. The lifespan of my ordinary ties is about two meals. Either I spill soy sauce or soup on it...

"If you wear an ordinary tie, I have to make sure the front piece is slightly longer than the back piece, otherwise the front piece is so long it goes right to my ankle, or I have to tuck it into my shirt."
Bow ties solve all these problems while respecting Tsang's fondness for fiscal prudence.
"Bow ties on the whole are cheaper than ordinary ties," he added.
President Jiang Zemin and Premier Li Peng will take a slow boat from China to the handover ceremony to avoid protesters.
The leaders will set sail from Kowloon, on the mainland, across the harbour to Wanchai on Hong Kong Island.
Jiang and Britain's Prince Charles will preside over Monday's midnight ceremony to mark the end of Britain's one-and-a-half centuries of rule.
Police have set up designated protest areas on land. Li is highly unpopular in Hong Kong because of his role in suppressing the 1989 student protests in Beijing's Tiananmen Square.
Security fears have denied Prince Charles a tram trip.
Handover organisers had planned for Britain's future king to take a common tram trip on the century-old line between the Central and Admiralty districts -- a favourite tourist jaunt.
The British Council said the outing was cancelled due to high security risks and traffic problems at the time of the handover.
Condom manufacturers believe the handover feel-good factor -- and a five-day holiday for Hong Kongers -- could boost sales by up to 20 percent.
"I think it is a great thing for Chinese people to celebrate the handover," said John Lam Fuk-sang, area manager for the Durex condom firm.
The South China Morning Post reported that in a poll of what people planned to do on June 30, six percent said they planned to be in bed by the midnight handover time.
Forget the Last Empress Barbie Doll and the rubber Chinese Dragon.

For the souvenir hunter who has already scooped up all the tacky memorabilia on offer for the handover, why not try a chunk of "barren rock" -- the dismissive title given to Hong Kong by 19th century Lord Palmerston when Britain took over the colony.
For HK$97 in Hong Kong's popular tourist Stanley Market, you can buy a chunk of granite in a wooden box with a colonial-type crest.
British Prime Minister Tony Blair has a Hong Kong Chinese sister-in-law and she will join his entourage when he flies in for the Hong Kong handover.
Katy Blair Tse Kam-har, who was sent to Britain by her parents as a student and stayed on, met her husband, the premier's brother Bill, while working at a London legal firm.
She founded a Chinese community centre in London 11 years ago. She will arrive back in her old home town with her husband on Blair's air force jet on Monday, but will pay her own way.
Hong Kong electric companies are beefing up their manpower to deal with handover ceremonies and celebrations.
More than 100 extra engineers will be on standby for the glittering event.
"It can be coped with. No problem." Hong Kong Electric said. "Every Christmas and Chinese New Year it's the same."
The red flag has been hoisted at Big Wave Bay, Stanley Main, Hair Pin, Middle Bay, Repulse Bay, St. Stephen's and South Bay beaches.
No, Chinese rule has not arrived early. It's merely a lifeguard alert.
The weather is inclement and it's dangerous to go swimming.
